hints: A queue only lets you take items from the front, but a stack must give back the newest item first. Could you rearrange the queue right after each push so the newest item is already at the front?

Use one queue. After adding x to the back, rotate the queue: remove from the front and re-add to the back size − 1 times. Now x is at the front, so pop and top are just 'remove front' and 'look at front'.

1. push(x): add x to the back.
  2. Then repeat size - 1 times: q.add(q.remove()).
  3. pop(): q.remove().
  4. top(): q.peek().
  5. empty(): q.isEmpty().

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Push normally; on pop/top, move all but the last item into a second queue, read the last one, then swap the queues.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: One queue rotated after every push so the newest item is always at the front.

explain: In the sample, push 4 gives [4]. push 9 gives [4, 9], then one rotation moves 4 behind: [9, 4]. top returns the front, 9, and pop removes 9 leaving [4], so empty is false. The invariant: the queue's front-to-back order is always the stack's top-to-bottom order. Either push or pop has to pay O(n); putting the cost on push keeps the other three operations O(1).
recognize: Build a LIFO structure from a FIFO queue → rotate the queue after each push.
